out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at kitchen handwashing sink used by food employees.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. EHS instructed the manager to provide a hand washing sign at the kitchen hand sink. PIC provided temporary handwashing signage at the kitchen sink and ordered a permanent handwashing sign.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: squeeze bottles of oil, different type of sauces stored on cook line and throughout establishment.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs. PIC labeled squeeze bottles for all aforementioned food items.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter throughout the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. PIC placed wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: Observed no date marking for meat sauce, diced tomato, fried chicken in WIC that had been held for more than 24 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC understands all cooked/prepared foods kept for more than 24 hours must be date marked. PIC has date marked the aforementioned food items accordingly.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Restriction & Storage; Medicines Not Necessary
violations.observation: Observed employee’s supplements were stored on the shelf above the dough station.
violations.corrective_action: Medicines that are not necessary for the health of employees present an unjustified risk to the health of other employees and consumers and shall be removed from the establishment. The supplements were removed from the prep area and moved to the designated area by PIC.

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Test Kit/Device for Chemical Sanitizer
violations.observation: There is no test kit located in the facility for monitoring the concentration of the chemical sanitizing solutions from dispenser at 3-compartment sink. (quaternary ammonia)
violations.corrective_action: PIC purchased a quaternary ammonia test kit during inspection.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: pickles at 47F, blue cheese crumbles at 50 F in 2 DR prep cooler (R) and sliced ham at 55 F, chicken wings at 48 F, sliced provolone cheese at 51F in 2 DR prep cooler (L)
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC discarded pickles, blue cheese crumbles, chicken wings, sliced ham and sliced provolone cheese. PIC relocated other TCS food items, which had been stored in the cooler for no more than 4 hours, to another unit maintaining the proper temperature.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: 2 DR prep cooler (R) at 44 F and prep cooler (L) at 45 F.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. PIC discontinued use of the 2 DR prep cooler (R) and 2 DR prep cooler (L) and contacted a technician during the inspection. PIC will email proof of the repairs to EHS.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: Observed no date marking for lasagna, fried chicken, grilled chicken and etc. in WIC that have been kept for more than 24 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC understands all cooked/prepared foods kept for more than 24 hours must be date marked. PIC has date marked the aforementioned food items accordingly.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED MARINARA SAUCE AT 90-147F IN HOT HOLDING WELL.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC REHEATED SAUCE TO 165F AND UNDERSTANDS HOT HOLDING FOODS MUST REMAIN AT 135F CONSISTENTLY THROUGHOUT THE FOOD.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food items were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED FETA AT 45F AND ALFREDO SAUCE AT 45F IN RIGHT 2-DOOR PREP-TOP.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC MOVED FOODS TO FREEZER TO DROP TEMPERATURE DURING INSPECTION AND UNDERSTANDS COLD HOLDING FOODS MUST BE KEPT AT 41F OR BELOW.
